{{grievance_nature}}

{{resolution_sought}}

letter:
FORMAL LETTER BEFORE ACTION: UNLAWFUL DEDUCTION FROM WAGES
PURSUANT TO SECTION 13 OF THE EMPLOYMENT RIGHTS ACT 1996

Date: {{date}}

TO: Payroll & HR Department, {{employer_name}}
FROM: {{employee_name}} (Payroll Ref: {{payroll_ref}})
SUBJECT: FORMAL DEMAND FOR PAYMENT OF OUTSTANDING WAGES (£{{amount_owed}})

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am writing to formally place you on notice regarding unpaid remuneration due to me for the following period: {{pay_period}}.

1. PARTICULARS OF ARREARS:
- Unpaid / deducted working time: {{hours_worked}}
- Total gross amount unlawfully withheld: £{{amount_owed}}
- Relevant payslip references: {{pay_period}}

2. STATUTORY BREACH:
Under Section 13(1) of the Employment Rights Act 1996, an employer shall not make a deduction from wages of a worker employed by him unless the deduction is required or authorised by statute or by a relevant provision of the worker's contract previously notified in writing.

I have not provided written consent for any deduction, nor does any statutory exception apply. The withholding of payment for hours legitimately worked constitutes an unlawful deduction from wages.

3. FORMAL DEMAND:
Please arrange for the full sum of £{{amount_owed}} to be paid into my bank account within 7 calendar days of the date of this letter:
Nominated Account: {{bank_details}}

Additionally, please issue an amended itemised pay statement (payslip) reflecting this payment pursuant to Section 8 of the Employment Rights Act 1996.

4. LEGAL ESCALATION WARNING:
If this sum is not paid within 7 calendar days, I will immediately register this dispute with ACAS for Early Conciliation, preparatory to submitting an ET1 Claim to the Employment Tribunal. Please be advised that an Employment Tribunal has statutory power to order full repayment together with compensation for financial losses incurred.

Yours faithfully,

{{employee_name}}
Worker / Union Member

letter:
FORMAL STATUTORY DEMAND FOR STATUTORY SICK PAY (SSP)
PURSUANT TO PART XI OF THE SOCIAL SECURITY CONTRIBUTIONS AND BENEFITS ACT 1992

Date: {{date}}

TO: Payroll Department, {{employer_name}}
FROM: {{employee_name}}
SUBJECT: WITHHELD STATUTORY SICK PAY (£{{ssp_amount}}) - FORMAL DEMAND

Dear Payroll Manager,

I am writing to formally challenge the non-payment of Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) due to me for the period of incapacity: {{sickness_period}}.

1. STATUTORY ENTITLEMENT CRITERIA MET:
I confirm that I meet all statutory conditions for SSP eligibility under Section 151 of the Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992:
- Period of Incapacity for Work (PIW) exceeds four consecutive calendar days.
- My average weekly earnings exceed the statutory Lower Earnings Limit (LEL) of £123.00 per week.
- Qualifying Days: {{qualifying_days}}.
- Timely medical evidence was provided: {{fit_note_details}}.

2. ILLEGALITY OF WITHHOLDING SSP:
SSP is a mandatory statutory entitlement. An employer cannot lawfully refuse SSP because a worker is engaged via an agency, on a zero-hours contract, or has recently started employment, provided the earnings threshold is satisfied.

3. DEMAND FOR PAYMENT OR FORM SSP1:
Please confirm in writing within 5 working days that the sum of £{{ssp_amount}} will be disbursed in the next pay cycle.

If you dispute my entitlement, you are legally required under Regulation 15 of the Statutory Sick Pay (General) Regulations 1982 to furnish me immediately with an official HMRC Form SSP1 ('Statutory Sick Pay and an employee's claim for benefit'), stating your precise statutory reasons for refusal, so that I may lodge a formal dispute with HMRC's Statutory Payments Dispute Team.

Yours faithfully,

{{employee_name}}
Employee / Agency Worker

letter:
STATUTORY NOTICE OF RIGHT TO BE ACCOMPANIED
PURSUANT TO SECTION 10 OF THE EMPLOYMENT RELATIONS ACT 1999

Date: {{date}}

TO: HR & Disciplining Manager, {{employer_name}}
FROM: {{employee_name}}
SUBJECT: STATUTORY NOTICE OF COMPANION FOR {{hearing_type}} ON {{hearing_date}}

Dear Management,

I refer to your notification requiring me to attend a {{hearing_type}} currently scheduled for:
Date & Time: {{hearing_date}}.

1. EXERCISE OF ABSOLUTE STATUTORY RIGHT:
Pursuant to Section 10(1) of the Employment Relations Act 1999, a worker has an absolute statutory right to be accompanied at any disciplinary or grievance hearing by a certified trade union official or workplace colleague.

I formally notify you that I will be accompanied at this hearing by:
Companion: {{companion_name}}
Affiliation: {{union_name}}.

2. STATUTORY POWERS OF THE COMPANION:
In accordance with Section 10(2B) of the Employment Relations Act 1999 and the Employment Appeal Tribunal authority in Toal v GB Oils Ltd [2013], my companion is legally permitted to:
- Address the hearing and present my case.
- Sum up the submissions and respond on my behalf to any view expressed at the hearing.
- Confer privately with me at any point during the meeting.

3. REQUEST FOR POSTPONEMENT (IF REQUIRED):
If my chosen companion is unavailable at the time proposed, Section 10(4) and (5) obliges the employer to postpone the hearing to a reasonable alternative time within five working days proposed by the employee.

Please ensure all meeting documentation, CCTV footage, and witness statements are provided to me at least 48 hours prior to the hearing to allow adequate preparation with my representative.

Yours sincerely,

{{employee_name}}
Union Member

STATUTORY REQUEST FOR INFORMATION & EQUAL TREATMENT
PURSUANT TO REGULATION 5 & REGULATION 16 OF THE AGENCY WORKERS REGULATIONS 2010

Date: {{date}}

TO: Temporary Work Agency: {{agency_name}}
CC: Hirer: {{hirer_name}}
FROM: {{worker_name}}
SUBJECT: AWR EQUAL TREATMENT ENTITLEMENT COMPLIANCE NOTICE

Dear Sir or Madam,

I am engaged by {{agency_name}} on a temporary assignment at the premises of {{hirer_name}}, which commenced on {{start_date}}. To date, I have completed {{qualifying_weeks}} on this assignment in the same role without any disqualifying breaks in continuity.

1. QUALIFYING PERIOD COMPLETED:
In accordance with Regulation 7 of the Agency Workers Regulations 2010 (SI 2010/93), I have completed the 12-week qualifying period in this role.

2. STATUTORY ENTITLEMENT:
Under Regulation 5(1), an agency worker who has completed the qualifying period is entitled to the same basic working and employment conditions as if they had been recruited directly by the hirer to do the same job. This includes:
- Basic hourly pay and shift premia.
- Overtime calculation rates.
- Annual leave entitlements.

3. CURRENT DISPARITY:
{{disparity_details}}

4. FORMAL REQUEST FOR WRITTEN STATEMENT:
Under Regulation 16, I formally request a written statement setting out:
(a) The relevant terms and conditions applicable to a comparable permanent employee recruited directly by {{hirer_name}}.
(b) An explanation for any divergence in pay rates or benefits.
(c) Backdated reimbursement of the differential owed to me since the completion of my 12th week.

Regulation 16(3) stipulates that you must respond with this written statement within 28 days.

Yours faithfully,

{{worker_name}}
Agency Worker

PRINCIPAL STATEMENT OF TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT
CONTRACT OF EMPLOYMENT (ENGLAND & WALES)
ISSUED PURSUANT TO SECTION 1 OF THE EMPLOYMENT RIGHTS ACT 1996

DOCUMENT REFERENCE: UK-EMP-SECURE-2026
CLASSIFICATION: PRIVILEGED & CONFIDENTIAL EMPLOYMENT INSTRUMENT
ISSUED ON: {{date}}

PARTIES TO THIS AGREEMENT:
1. THE EMPLOYER:
   {{employer_name}}
   Registered Address: {{employer_address}}

2. THE EMPLOYEE:
   {{employee_name}}
   Residential Address: {{employee_address}}

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. COMMENCEMENT AND CONTINUOUS EMPLOYMENT
   1.1. The Employee's employment under this Agreement shall commence on: {{start_date}}.
   1.2. No period of previous employment with any other employer counts as part of the Employee's continuous service.

2. JOB TITLE AND DUTIES
   2.1. The Employee is engaged as: {{job_title}}.
   2.2. The Employee shall report to their assigned Operations Supervisor or Department Manager and perform the duties associated with this role with reasonable care, skill, and diligence.

3. PLACE OF WORK
   3.1. The Employee's primary place of work will be located at: {{work_location}}.
   3.2. The Employer reserves the right to reasonably require the Employee to work at other operational sites within a 15-mile travel radius upon reasonable prior notice.

4. REMUNERATION AND PAYMENT SCHEDULE
   4.1. The Employee's basic remuneration shall be: {{basic_pay}}.
   4.2. Remuneration is calculated weekly/monthly and shall be remitted directly by electronic BACS transfer into the Employee's nominated UK bank account.
   4.3. The Employer shall issue a comprehensive itemised pay statement (payslip) on or before each pay day pursuant to Section 8 of the Employment Rights Act 1996.
   4.4. Deductions: The Employer will make only statutory deductions for PAYE Income Tax, Class 1 National Insurance Contributions, and workplace pension contributions, unless specific written consent is provided in accordance with Section 13 ERA 1996.

5. WORKING HOURS & OVERTIME
   5.1. The Employee's normal working hours shall be: {{working_hours}}.
   5.2. Mandatory break entitlements shall comply strictly with Regulation 12 of the Working Time Regulations 1998 (uninterrupted rest breaks of not less than 20 minutes for shifts exceeding 6 hours).
   5.3. Overtime Policy: {{overtime_terms}}.

6. ANNUAL LEAVE AND PUBLIC HOLIDAYS
   6.1. The Employee is entitled to: {{holiday_entitlement}}.
   6.2. The statutory annual leave year runs from 1st January to 31st December.
   6.3. Unused statutory holiday allowance will be compensated pro-rata upon lawful termination of employment.

7. SICKNESS ABSENCE AND STATUTORY SICK PAY (SSP)
   7.1. In the event of incapacity due to illness or injury, the Employee must notify the Employer prior to the commencement of their scheduled shift.
   7.2. Sickness exceeding seven consecutive calendar days requires an official NHS Statement of Fitness for Work (Fit Note).
   7.3. Eligible employees will receive Statutory Sick Pay (SSP) in accordance with Part XI of the Social Security Contributions and Benefits Act 1992.

8. PENSION SCHEME (AUTO-ENROLMENT)
   8.1. Pursuant to the Pensions Act 2008, eligible jobholders will be automatically enrolled into the Employer's designated qualifying workplace pension scheme following the statutory postponement period.

9. DISCIPLINARY & GRIEVANCE PROCEDURES
   9.1. The disciplinary and grievance procedures applicable to this employment strictly mirror the ACAS statutory Code of Practice No. 1.
   9.2. The Employee has an absolute statutory right under Section 10 of the Employment Relations Act 1999 to be accompanied at any formal hearing by a certified Trade Union representative or colleague.

10. TERMINATION AND NOTICE PERIODS
   10.1. The notice required to terminate this employment by either party is: {{notice_period}}.
   10.2. Nothing in this clause prevents the Employer from summarily dismissing the Employee without notice in proven cases of gross misconduct.

letter:
ASSURED SHORTHOLD TENANCY AGREEMENT (AST)
FOR RESIDENTIAL PROPERTY IN ENGLAND & WALES
PURSUANT TO PART I OF THE HOUSING ACT 1988 (AS AMENDED)

DOCUMENT REFERENCE: UK-AST-SECURE-2026
STANDARD FORM LEASE COMPLIANT WITH THE TENANT FEES ACT 2019
DATE OF EXECUTION: {{date}}

THIS AGREEMENT IS MADE BETWEEN:
1. THE LANDLORD:
   {{landlord_name}}
   Notice Address (pursuant to s.48 Landlord and Tenant Act 1987): {{landlord_address}}

2. THE TENANT(S):
   {{tenant_name}}

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
OPERATIVE TERMS OF THE TENANCY
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

1. THE PROPERTY
   The Landlord agrees to let and the Tenant agrees to take the residential dwelling known as:
   Address: {{property_address}} ("the Premises"), together with all landlord fixtures, furniture, and fittings listed in the check-in inventory.

2. TERM AND RENT
   2.1. The Tenancy shall be for a fixed term of: {{tenancy_term}}, commencing on: {{start_date}}.
   2.2. The Rent shall be: £{{monthly_rent}} per calendar month.
   2.3. Rent is payable in advance on the: {{rent_due_day}}, by standing order into the Landlord's designated bank account.
   2.4. Utility and Local Tax arrangements: {{bills_included}}.

3. SECURITY DEPOSIT & STATUTORY PROTECTION
   3.1. The Tenant shall pay a security deposit of: £{{deposit_amount}}.
   3.2. Compliance with Housing Act 2004: In accordance with Sections 213-214 of the Housing Act 2004 and the Tenant Fees Act 2019, the Deposit will be secured within 30 days of receipt in an authorized government scheme:
        Custodial Scheme: {{deposit_scheme}}.
   3.3. Prescribed Information will be issued to the Tenant within 30 days of receiving the deposit.
   3.4. The deposit cannot be withheld arbitrarily and will be refunded upon termination subject only to documented damage beyond reasonable wear and tear or rent arrears.

4. TENANT'S OBLIGATIONS
   4.1. Pay the rent punctually at the times specified.
   4.2. Keep the interior of the Premises clean, well-ventilated, and in good order throughout the tenancy.
   4.3. Not cause nuisance, annoyance, or anti-social behaviour to occupiers of neighbouring properties.
   4.4. Not assign, underlet, or share possession of the Premises without prior written consent from the Landlord (consent not to be unreasonably withheld).
   4.5. Permit the Landlord or their authorised contractors access to inspect or conduct statutory repairs upon at least 24 hours written notice, except in genuine emergencies.

5. LANDLORD'S STATUTORY OBLIGATIONS
   5.1. Repair Covenant: Pursuant to Section 11 of the Landlord and Tenant Act 1985 and the Homes (Fitness for Human Habitation) Act 2018, the Landlord shall keep in repair:
        (a) The structure and exterior of the dwelling-house (including drains, gutters, and external pipes).
        (b) The installations for the supply of water, gas, electricity, and sanitation (including basins, sinks, baths, and sanitary conveniences).
        (c) The installations for space heating and heating water.
   5.2. Safety Compliance: The Landlord warrants compliance with the Gas Safety (Installation and Use) Regulations 1998 (annual CP12 certificate) and the Electrical Safety Standards in the Private Rented Sector (England) Regulations 2020 (EICR report).
   5.3. Quiet Enjoyment: The Landlord covenants that the Tenant paying the rent shall peaceably and quietly possess and enjoy the Premises without unlawful interruption.

6. PROHIBITED PAYMENTS (TENANT FEES ACT 2019)
   In compliance with the Tenant Fees Act 2019, the Landlord and Agent confirm that no prohibited fees (including administration fees, viewing fees, inventory fees, or renewal fees) have been or will be charged to the Tenant.

7. DETERMINATION AND NOTICES
   7.1. Any statutory notice served under Section 21 or Section 8 of the Housing Act 1988 must strictly comply with prescribed statutory notice periods.
   7.2. The Tenant may terminate the tenancy at the expiration of the fixed term by serving not less than one calendar month's notice in writing.

══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SIGNATURES OF THE PARTIES

titleEn: Holiday Pay & Annual Leave Entitlement Claim
titlePl: Wezwanie: Zaległe Holiday Pay i Urlop
titleRo: Cerere Plată Concediu de Odihnă (Holiday Pay)
statutoryReference: Working Time Regulations 1998, regs 13, 13A, 14 & 16
descriptionEn: Claim unpaid holiday pay or refused statutory leave (5.6 weeks), including regular overtime in the holiday rate.
descriptionPl: Żądanie wypłaty zaległego holiday pay lub udzielenia ustawowego urlopu (5,6 tyg.) – z uwzględnieniem regularnych nadgodzin w stawce.
descriptionRo: Cerere pentru plata concediului restant sau acordarea celor 5,6 săptămâni legale.

descriptionPl: Rezygnacja z pracy z zachowaniem okresu wypowiedzenia oraz żądaniem ostatniej wypłaty, ekwiwalentu za urlop i P45.
descriptionRo: Demisie cu preaviz și cerere pentru ultimul salariu, concediu neefectuat și P45.

descriptionPl: Odwołanie od zwolnienia lub ostrzeżenia: wadliwa procedura, brak dowodów lub nieproporcjonalna kara.
descriptionRo: Contestație: procedură incorectă, lipsă de dovezi sau sancțiune disproporționată.

descriptionPl: Agencje nie mogą pobierać opłat za znalezienie pracy (rejestracja, CV, 'depozyty' szkoleniowe). Żądanie zwrotu.
